The '''2014–15 Ligue 1''' season was the 77th season since its establishment. [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the two-time defending champions and successfully defended their title.

==Teams==
There were 20 clubs in the league, with three promoted teams from [[Ligue 2]] replacing the three teams that were relegated from [[Ligue 1]] following the [[2013–14 Ligue 1|2013–14 season]]. All clubs that secured Ligue 1 status for the season were subject to approval by the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]] before becoming eligible to participate.

[[FC Metz|Metz]] was the first team to win promotion from [[Ligue 2]] after a 3–0 victory against [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]] at the [[Stade de l'Abbé-Deschamps]], ending a six-year span in the lower divisions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Metz-en-l1/460117|title=Metz en L1 !|trans-title=Metz in L1!|publisher=[[L'Équipe|lequipe.fr]]|language=fr|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref> [[RC Lens|Lens]] returned to the top level after a 2–0 victory against [[CA Bastia]] on 16 May 2014 and finished a three-year span in 2nd level. Finally, [[SM Caen|Caen]] returned  for the first time in two years following a 2–2 draw with [[Dijon FCO|Dijon]] on 16 May 2014.

{{smalldiv|1=
* <sup>1</sup>Due to Stade Michel d'Ornano hosting the [[2014 FEI World Equestrian Games]], Caen will host its two first home games at [[MMArena]] in [[Le Mans]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Campagne d'abonnement saison 2014/2015 ! |url=http://www.smcaen.fr/liste-saisons/saison-2013-2014/actualites/club/campagne-dabonnement-saison-2014-2015 |publisher=smcaen.fr |date=12 June 2014 |access-date=12 June 2014 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140709071643/http://www.smcaen.fr/liste-saisons/saison-2013-2014/actualites/club/campagne-dabonnement-saison-2014-2015 |archive-date=9 July 2014 }}</ref>
* <sup>2</sup>Lens home stadium, [[Stade Félix-Bollaert]] will be closed for the entire season, due to a renovation in preparation for [[UEFA Euro 2016]]. Lens will play their home games in various venues which are to be determined.<ref>{{cite news|title=Le RC Lens cherche un stade : " Si on ne s’entend pas, ce sera Bienvenue chez les cons " |url=http://www.lavoixdunord.fr/sports/le-rc-lens-cherche-un-stade-si-on-ne-s-entend-pas-ia182b205n1882957 |publisher=La Voix du Nord |date=30 January 2014 |access-date=1 June 2014 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140423023244/http://www.lavoixdunord.fr/sports/le-rc-lens-cherche-un-stade-si-on-ne-s-entend-pas-ia182b205n1882957 |archive-date=23 April 2014 }}</ref>
* <sup>3</sup>The [[Stade Vélodrome]] is currently undergoing renovation in preparation for [[UEFA Euro 2016]]. The stadium will be completed in time for the 2014-15 season, where capacity will be 67,000 - up from 48,000 the previous season.<ref>{{cite news|title=La ville de Marseille et la société Arema signent un contrat pour la reconfiguration du stade Vélodrome|url=http://www.francebtp.com/infrastructures/article/2010/11/08/45525/la-ville-marseille-societe-arema-signent-contrat-pour-reconfiguration-stade-velodrome.php|publisher=France BTP|date=21 June 2011|access-date=26 September 2011|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325034306/http://www.francebtp.com/infrastructures/article/2010/11/08/45525/la-ville-marseille-societe-arema-signent-contrat-pour-reconfiguration-stade-velodrome.php|archive-date=25 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* <sup>4</sup>The [[Stade Geoffroy-Guichard]] is currently undergoing renovation in preparation for [[UEFA Euro 2016]]. The current capacity is 38,458, the final capacity will be 41,965.
* <sup>5</sup>The [[Stadium Municipal]] is currently undergoing renovation in preparation for [[UEFA Euro 2016]]. The current capacity is not published yet but is a decrease from the original capacity of 35,470.
}}
